design.text: Open-label, randomized, multicenter, parallel-group, active-controlled study with three treatment arms (degarelix 240/160 mg, degarelix 240/80 mg, and leuprolide 7.5 mg) for 12 months.

citations.quote: The safety and efficacy of degarelix were assessed in an open-label, randomized, multicenter, parallel-group study in patients with prostate cancer. A total of 620 patients were randomized to receive one of the following three treatment regimens for 12 months.

Patients assigned to the two degarelix arms received the same starting dose 240 mg at a concentration of 40 mg/ml subcutaneously, followed by monthly maintenance doses of either 160 mg at a concentration of 40 mg/ml or 80 mg at a concentration of 20 mg/ml starting 28 days after the initiation dosing. Patients assigned to the leuprolide arm received the same doses of 7.5 mg intramuscularly for both treatment initiation and monthly maintenance.

population.text: Patients with prostate cancer; 20% had metastatic disease and 80% had non-metastatic disease (locally advanced, localized, or PSA relapse only after primary definitive therapy).

citations.quote: Of the patients randomized, 20% had metastatic disease and 80% had non-metastatic disease, including locally advanced disease, localized disease, and PSA relapse only disease after primary definitive therapy. Approximately 81% of patients completed the 12-month treatments.

endpoint.text: Probability of testosterone ≤ 0.5 ng/mL from Day 28 to Day 364 in each arm.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was to evaluate the probability of testosterone \le 0.5 ng/mL from Day 28 to Day 364 in each of the three arms.

n.text: 610 patients in the active-controlled analysis (degarelix 240/160 mg N=202, degarelix 240/80 mg N=207, leuprolide 7.5 mg N=201).

citations.quote: TRADENAME was studied in an active-controlled trial (N = 610) in which patients with prostate cancer were randomized to receive TRADENAME (subcutaneous) or leuprolide (intramuscular) monthly for 12 months.
ITT analysis set	202	207	201

result.text: Probability of medical castration (testosterone ≤ 0.5 ng/mL, Day 28–364) was 98.3% (95% CI 94.8–99.4%) for degarelix 240/160 mg, 97.2% (93.5–98.8%) for degarelix 240/80 mg, and 96.4% (92.5–98.2%) for leuprolide 7.5 mg.

citations.quote: The results demonstrated that the probabilities of medical castration were 98.3% (95% CI: 94.8% - 99.4%), 97.2% (93.5% - 98.8%) and 96.4% (92.5% - 98.2%) for the degarelix 240/160 mg, degarelix 240/80 mg and leuprolide 7.5 mg arms, respectively, indicating that degarelix is effective in achieving and maintaining efficacious biochemical castration during 12 months treatment.

indication.text: GnRH receptor antagonist indicated for treatment of patients with advanced prostate cancer.

citations.quote: TRADENAME is a GnRH receptor antagonist indicated for treatment of patients with advanced prostate cancer.

target_moa.text: Degarelix is a GnRH receptor antagonist that binds reversibly to pituitary GnRH receptors, reducing release of gonadotropins and consequently testosterone.

citations.quote: Degarelix is a GnRH receptor antagonist. It binds reversibly to the pituitary GnRH receptors, thereby reducing the release of gonadotropins and consequently testosterone.
Degarelix is a synthetic linear decapeptide amide containing seven unnatural amino acids, five of which are D-amino acids.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were injection site reactions, hot flashes, increased weight, and transaminase/GGT increases. Injection site adverse events occurred in 35% (240/80 mg arm) vs <1% leuprolide; hot flash 26% vs 21% leuprolide. Injection site pain 28%, erythema 17%, swelling 6%.

Study CS21 was an open-label, randomized, active-controlled, three-arm, international, phase 3 trial of monthly degarelix vs leuprolide (Lupron Depot) in patients with prostate cancer in whom androgen deprivation therapy was warranted.
